annotations.note: Identification citation: quantum phase estimation cited to the standard textbook, which presents the algorithm. Requiring the words 'Hamiltonian diagonalization' is too literal.
Co-cited with [20]. [21] is about subspace expansion and orbital relaxation, not ansatz design, though it notes that variational methods adapt naturally to device parameters.

Filter diagonalization (small Hamiltonian matrix built from real-time-propagated states) is exactly the classical ancestor of solving generalized eigenproblems from real-time evolution; cited in a group of four. 'Possibly the wrong reference' is wrong.
One of four works cited for gathering information from real-time evolution: [27] is the Lanczos real-time evolution method this line of work builds on. It is not expected to mention VQPE.
The cited work analyses the success and failure probability of LCU constructions; the 'flagged state' and 'target amplitude' framing is the citing paper's own application.

Cited for why ill-conditioned generalized eigenproblems are numerically unstable, which is the cited work's subject (condition numbers and backward error of GEPs); the truncation rule itself is the citing authors' method.

Caused by the checker: the reference is a 2020 Springer workshop volume ('Orthogonal Polynomials: 2nd AIMS-Volkswagen Stiftung Workshop'), but the resolver matched the generic title to a different survey called 'Orthogonal Polynomials', which was then checked.
Childs and Wiebe do give the success probability of LCU; 'where Ex specifies the center of spectral decay' is the citing paper's own notation for its application, not a claim about the source.
